explanations.explanation: The message says, "Ask the LORD for rain in springtime." He's the One who makes the storm clouds, and He will give everyone showers of rain and crops in the field. Friend, that's asking the owner of the oven about the oven. Nobody in the line has to pass the message along.
Priests aren't in this verse at all, baker. The verse says, "Ask the LORD for rain in springtime." The One to ask is the One who makes the storm clouds. Nobody stands in between.

No king shows up in this verse. The message sends the people straight to the LORD: "Ask the LORD for rain in springtime." He makes the storm clouds and gives the showers. A king can't take over a job that belongs to Him.

Close, but the message says the opposite. It says idols speak deceit and diviners see illusions. They tell false dreams and offer empty comfort. Comfort that's empty is like a cookie jar with a nice label and nothing inside.
That's right, baker. The message says idols speak deceit and diviners see illusions. They tell false dreams and offer empty comfort. They sound comforting, but there's nothing real behind it.

That's the word, friend. The people wander like sheep, "oppressed for lack of a shepherd." Sheep without a shepherd have nobody guiding them. Remember that word, because the LORD picks it up in the very next verse.

The verse doesn't say anything about a pasture running out. It says the people wander like sheep, "oppressed for lack of a shepherd." What's missing is the person leading them. I think a field with no shepherd is still a long walk with no direction.
No fence in this verse, baker. The text says the people wander like sheep, "oppressed for lack of a shepherd." It's a shepherd they lack, not a barrier. A fence can't lead anybody anywhere.

That's what He says: "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders." This is a heavy part, friend. Notice that it comes right after the people were left wandering like sheep. The next line turns toward the flock.
The LORD doesn't say He'll warn them here. He says, "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders." The word is punish. It's a heavy line, and it's good to read it plainly.

Testing isn't mentioned in this verse. The LORD says, "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders." The word is punish, baker. It's a heavy moment, and the text doesn't soften it.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "He will make them like His royal steed in battle." This is the same flock that was wandering with no shepherd. I'd have a hard time believing a sheep could hear that without checking the mirror twice.
No lion here, friend. The LORD says He will make them "like His royal steed in battle." That's a warhorse that belongs to the King. Lions and forests never come up in this verse.
The verse never mentions an eagle. It says the LORD "will make them like His royal steed in battle." So it's a horse, and a royal one. Nothing about the sky.
That's it. "The cornerstone will come from Judah." The LORD also says the tent peg, the battle bow and every ruler come from him. Judah is the house the LORD just said He attends to like a flock.
Benjamin isn't named here, baker. The verse says, "The cornerstone will come from Judah." That's the same Judah as the flock the LORD just spoke of. The cornerstone and the tent peg come from him.

Levi doesn't show up in this verse. The LORD says, "The cornerstone will come from Judah." The tent peg, the battle bow and every ruler are tied to Judah too. Easy to mix up when so many names float around.
True, baker. The text says, "They will fight because the LORD is with them." He's the reason they fight at all. Nothing about it depends on how tough they are on their own.
It's actually true, friend. The text says, "They will fight because the LORD is with them." The reason is that He's with them. The verse also says they'll put the horsemen to shame.

That's the reason He gives: "I will restore them because I have compassion on them." Compassion is the whole answer. He doesn't hand them a bill first, baker. I'll take that over a warranty card any day.
The LORD doesn't say they earned it. He says, "I will restore them because I have compassion on them." The reason is His compassion. Nobody here is paying a debt off.
Keeping the law isn't the reason in this verse. The LORD says, "I will restore them because I have compassion on them." Compassion is His stated reason, friend. Nothing about a perfect record.
True. The LORD says, "For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them." That's a promise to Judah and Joseph, not a maybe. Being answered by your own God is a good thing to hear.
It's actually true, baker. The LORD says, "For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them." That's right in the verse. He promises to answer.

Yes. "Their children will see it and be joyful; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD." The gladness isn't kept to one generation. The kids get to watch it happen, and I think that's a gift for the whole family.

Neighbors don't come up in this verse. It says, "Their children will see it and be joyful; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD." The ones who see and rejoice are the children. Nobody from next door is mentioned.
The verse doesn't say enemies, friend. It says, "Their children will see it and be joyful; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD." So it's the children who rejoice. Enemies aren't in the picture.

That's what He says: "I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them." The whistle comes because they're already redeemed. He's calling people who belong to Him. That's a good reason to come running, baker.

Repenting isn't the reason given. The LORD says, "I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them." The reason is that He has redeemed them. The text says nothing about them doing something first.
The nations aren't the reason here, friend. The LORD says, "I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them." It's His redeeming that brings the whistle. No nation is credited.
That's the word. "Though I sow them among the nations, they will remember Me in distant lands." Far away, they still remember Him. Even sown across the nations, they don't lose Him.
The verse says the opposite, baker. "Though I sow them among the nations, they will remember Me in distant lands." Distance doesn't erase it. They remember Him.

Doubt isn't the word in this verse. The LORD says, "Though I sow them among the nations, they will remember Me in distant lands." So it's remembering, friend. And the same verse says they and their children will live and return.
That's it. "I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon until no more room is found for them." The people come back in such numbers that space runs out. That's a good problem to have, baker.
Water isn't what runs out here. The LORD says, "I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon until no more room is found for them." It's room that runs out, friend. There are just that many of them.

Grain doesn't come up in this verse. The LORD says, "I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon until no more room is found for them." The word is room. So many people coming home that Gilead and Lebanon fill up.

explanations.answer: Assyria's pride falls and Egypt's scepter departs
explanations.explanation: Right. "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." Assyria's pride comes down and Egypt's scepter leaves. Those two names come up again after the LORD said He'd gather His people from there.

explanations.answer: Assyria's king repents and Egypt's king bows
explanations.explanation: The verse doesn't say that, baker. It says, "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." No repenting and no bowing. Assyria's pride comes down and Egypt's scepter goes.

explanations.answer: Assyria's army joins them and Egypt's gates open
explanations.explanation: Not in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." Nobody joins and no gates open. Assyria's pride falls and Egypt's scepter departs.
Not quite, baker. The LORD says, "I will strengthen them in the LORD, and in His name they will walk." The strength comes from Him, and they walk in His name. Own strength isn't in the verse.
That's right. The LORD says, "I will strengthen them in the LORD, and in His name they will walk." Their strength comes from Him. They walk in His name, not their own.
